question: what are the admission requirements for the school of business and public administration
answer: SBPA admits students on UTG's minimum requirements: WASSCE/GCE passes at credit level in 5 subjects including English, Mathematics and at least one commercial/business studies course for the intended programme. A credit in Statistics can be substituted for a Mathematics deficiency for admission into the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management. Mature students are admitted on four criteria: at least three credit passes in WASSCE/GCE, a minimum age of 30, five or more years of work experience, and some professional courses done as part of post-secondary education.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 3

question: what are the entry requirements and grades needed for bsc procurement and supply chain management
answer: The minimum admission requirements are WASSCE/GCE 'O' Level passes at credit level in five subjects including English Language, Mathematics and three relevant subjects, or equivalent qualifications. Exceptions may be made case by case for mature students who have been out of school for 5 years or more and can show they are prepared for university-level work. Admission decisions are final and not subject to appeal, but applicants who were not admitted may reapply the next academic year.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 5

question: can i get advanced standing in procurement and supply chain management
answer: Advanced standing may be granted case by case on admission with higher qualifications, such as the Advanced Level GCE in Accounting, the Technician Stage of AAT and CAT, partial ACCA, CIPS or CIMA qualifications or an equivalent, as well as other university-level courses done elsewhere.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 5

question: how long and how many years does the procurement and supply chain management degree take
answer: The programme runs for 8 semesters (4 years) as a minimum, with a course load of between 120 and 126 credit hours. The maximum time to complete the undergraduate programme is 7 years, and failing to finish within that time leads to expulsion. Where course waivers are given for credit transfers, it may take less than four years depending on how many waivers the student gets.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 3

question: how many credit hours do i need to graduate in procurement and supply chain management
answer: An honours degree needs a minimum of 126 semester hours (120 credit hours for an ordinary degree), made up of: University (General) required courses 33; Faculty compulsory courses 21; Programme core courses 54; Elective courses 12; Research Project and Dissertation 6. Total: 126 credit hours.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 5

question: do i need to write a research project thesis or dissertation to graduate with honours in procurement
answer: Yes. Students who want to graduate with honours (BSc Hons.) must do a research project or thesis worth 6 credit hours. Other students take two more elective courses to replace the six credits. The research paper for BSc management candidates should be at least 10,000 words. Work on the dissertation starts in the first semester of year 4 and continues into the second semester to make up the 6 credit hours.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 5-6, 9

question: can i do a minor with procurement and supply chain management
answer: Yes. All students of the programme have the option to minor in Finance, Economics, Management, Marketing, HRM, Tourism or any other discipline of interest. To graduate, a student must complete the University and Faculty requirements together with the required core courses.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 6

question: what are the requirements for an honours degree at utg school of business
answer: To be awarded an Honours Degree at UTG a student must have a CQPA of 3.500 or above. The award needs 40 courses: 11 general education requirements, 7 faculty requirements, a minimum of 18 core and 4 elective courses, plus a 6-credit Dissertation, giving at least 126 credit hours. Students may take courses missed in lower years, but not courses higher than their year of study. Only students who got an F in a course may repeat it.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 9

question: what is the grading system at the school of business and public administration
answer: SBPA undergraduate grades (score, grade, grade points, rating): 90-100 A+ 4.300 Excellent; 80-89 A 4.000 Excellent; 70-79 A- 3.700 Excellent; 67-69 B+ 3.300 Good; 64-66 B 3.000 Good; 60-63 B- 2.700 Good; 57-59 C+ 2.300 Satisfactory; 54-56 C 2.000 Satisfactory; 50-53 C- 1.700 Marginal Pass; 40-49 D 1.000 Marginal Pass; 0-39 F 0.000 Fail. The University issues letter grades and calculates student averages from the grade points.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 2

question: what is the pass mark and what score is a fail at the school of business
answer: In the SBPA grading system a score of 40-49 is a D (1.000 grade points, Marginal Pass), 50-53 is a C- (1.700, Marginal Pass), and a score of 0-39 is an F (0.000, Fail). Only students who obtained an F in a course are allowed to repeat it.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 2, 9

question: what gpa or cqpa do i need for first class honours
answer: A Bachelor Degree with Honours gets the distinction 'First Class' when the Cumulative Quality Point Average (CQPA) is at least 4.0; otherwise the Honours degree is awarded without special distinction. To be awarded an Honours Degree at all, a student needs a CQPA of 3.500 or above.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 2, 9

question: what cqpa do i need for summa cum laude magna cum laude or cum laude
answer: Distinctions at graduation are based on the Cumulative Quality Point Average (CQPA): Summa cum laude 4.00-4.30; Magna cum laude 3.85-3.99; Cum laude 3.70-3.84. A Bachelor Degree with Honours gets the distinction 'First Class' when the CQPA is at least 4.0; otherwise the Honours degree is awarded without special distinction.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 2

question: what are the general education requirements ger courses at utg
answer: The General Education Requirements are 11 courses (33 credit hours): MGT 110 Introduction to Management; INFO 111 Introduction to Information Technology; FRE 101 Introduction to French (French 1); ENG 101 Use of English 1; ENG 102 Use of English 2; GER 101 Humanistic Traditions (Cultural Studies); GER 100 One Language Course (Arabic, Spanish or Mandarin); a first and a second Social Science course (POL/PSY/SOC 101: Political Science, Psychology or Sociology); FRE 102 French 2; and GER 102 Gender/Literature/Concept of Education in Islam/Christian Religious Knowledge.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 6

question: what are the faculty requirements for the school of business and public administration
answer: All students take 7 Faculty Requirements courses (21 credit hours, 3 each): ECO 110 Principles of Microeconomics; ECO 120 Principles of Macroeconomics; ACC 110 Principles of Accounting I; ACC 120 Principles of Accounting II; ECO 211/MGT 211 Introduction to Statistical Methods for Economics 1/Business 1; ECO 210/MGT 210 Applied Mathematics for Economics/Business; and MKT 210 Principles of Marketing.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 6-7

question: can i transfer credits to the school of business and public administration from another university
answer: Students from other recognized institutions may transfer no more than 50% of the UTG course requirements from other reputable universities, as approved by the UTG Senate, in any degree programme at SBPA. Only comparable courses with similar content and level can be credited. The final decision rests entirely with SBPA and the UTG Senate.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 9

question: does the school of business and public administration offer internships
answer: SBPA works to give students internship opportunities in existing and emerging business organizations across The Gambia, and possibly other Sub-Saharan African countries. Throughout their coursework students are exposed to problem solving in the context of developing countries through real projects done with organizations in the local community.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 9

question: what jobs careers and career opportunities can i get with a degree in procurement and supply chain management
answer: Graduates can work as Supply Chain Managers, Logistics Analysts, Directors of Supplier Quality and Procurement, Chief Procurement Officers, Supply Management Analysts, New Product Procurement Planners and Strategic Sourcing Managers, among other careers. Students are expected to join the fast-growing financial sector as well as agriculture, tourism and other production and services organizations, and some are recruited before completing their course. SBPA collaborates with the Gambia Public Procurement Authority (GPPA) to create opportunities for these students.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 4-5

question: what is the procurement and supply chain management qualification intended to prepare you for
answer: The qualification prepares people to perform a broad range of complex technical procurement and supply activities, including preparing departmental budgets and planning and managing inventory; to manage physical, human and financial resources; to conduct research and consultancy; to write reports; and to analyse financial statements. It also prepares people to manage national and international procurement and supply activities, formulate policies and resolve disputes, in both the private and public sectors.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 4

question: what are the prerequisites for procurement and supply chain management psm courses
answer: Prerequisites stated in the curriculum: PSM 201 Theory of Government Procurement in The Gambia needs Introduction to Procurement and Supply Chain Management (PSM 200); PSM 300 The Practice of Public Procurement in The Gambia needs PSM 201; PSM 309 Global Purchasing and Supply Chain Management needs PSM 300; PSM 311 Procurement Ethics and Good Governance needs Introduction to Procurement (PSM 200); PSM 304 Sustainable Procurement needs PSM 311; FIN 220 Financial Management needs ACC 110 and ACC 120; ECO 224 Quantitative Methods needs ECO 210 and ECO 211.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 14-21

question: what is the full list of courses in the bsc procurement and supply chain management framework
answer: The BSc PSM framework runs over 8 semesters. Semester 1: ACC 110 Principles of Accounting I; ECON 110 Principles of Microeconomics; ECO 211/MGT 211 Introduction to Statistical Methods for Economics 1/Business 1; MGT 110 Principles of Management; INFO 111 Introduction to Information Technology; ENG 101 English (Use of English 1). Semester 2: ENG 102 English (Use of English 2); FRE 101 Introduction to French 1; ECON 120 Principles of Macroeconomics; GER 100 One Language Course (Arabic, Spanish or Mandarin); GER 101 Cultural Studies; POL/PSY/SOC 101 Political Science/Psychology/Sociology. Semester 3: MKT 210 Principles of Marketing; ECON 111 Applied Mathematics for Economics/Business Statistics; PSM 200 Introduction to Procurement; FIN 220 Financial Management; ACC 120 Principles of Accounting 2; POL/PSY/SOC 102 Political Science/Psychology/Sociology/Gender. Semester 4: PSM 210 Human Resource Issues in Procurement; PSM 201 Government Procurement in The Gambia; PSM 202 Understanding the Procurement Environment; LAW 210 Business Law; FRE 102 French 2; GER 102 Gender/Literature/Concept of Education in Islam/Christian Religious Knowledge. Semester 5: PSM 300 Practice Based Skills: Preparation of GPPA Documents; PSM 308 Communication in Procurement; MGT 311 Project Management; MGT 320 Research Methodology; PSM 306 Managerial Decision Making in Procurement; PSM 304 Sustainable Procurement. Semester 6: PSM 311 Procurement Ethics and Good Governance; PSM 305 Logistics and Distribution Management; MGT 320 Research Methodology; PSM 310 Legal Aspects in Purchasing and Supply Chain Management; ACC 312 Cost Accounting; MGT 313/PSM 313 Entrepreneurship Development/Small Business Management. Semester 7: PSM 317 Introduction to Procurement of Services; PSM 318 Operations Management; PSM 410 Strategic Procurement Management; PSM 309 Global Purchasing and Supply Chain Management; PSM 314 Negotiation in Purchasing and Supply; PSM 319 Stakeholder Relationships Management in Procurement and Supply. Semester 8: PSM 312 E-Procurement (procurement software applications); PSM 316 Contract Management in Procurement; PSM 320 Market Research/Analytics; PSM 315 Quality and Systems Management in Procurement and Supply; PSM 307 Inventory Management; ACC 491 Final Year Project Paper. Most courses are 3 credit hours; the Final Year Project Paper is 6. Note: the printed framework lists MGT 320 Research Methodology in both semester 5 and semester 6.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 11-13

question: what is mgt 110 introduction to management about
answer: MGT 110 Introduction to Management: This course introduces students to basic management functions. It covers basic concepts in management, management principles, the functions of the manager, planning, organization, span of management, departmentalization, line and staff authority and service departments; staffing and directing (selection, appraisal and development of managers), the nature of directing, motivation, leadership, controlling (the control process and control techniques), and management problems in The Gambia. It is scheduled in semester 1 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 6

question: what is info 111 introduction to information technology about
answer: INFO 111 Introduction to Information Technology: This course familiarizes students with basic concepts in information technology. Topics include the history and development of computer technology, the workings of the computer, computer types (analog, digital and hybrid), data transmission, data capture and validation (including error detection), systems analysis and design, and the programming process (problem definition, flow charting and decision tasks). It is scheduled in semester 1 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 6

question: what is eco 110 principles of microeconomics about
answer: ECO 110 Principles of Microeconomics: The definition, scope and methodology of economics; the economic problem of scarcity and choice; demand, supply and market equilibrium; the theory of costs; the theory of consumer behaviour; the behaviour of profit-maximizing firms; and the production process, including output decisions in the short run and the long run.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 7

question: what is eco 120 principles of macroeconomics about
answer: ECO 120 Principles of Macroeconomics: The definition, scope and method of macroeconomics versus microeconomics; measuring national output and national income; unemployment and inflation; aggregate expenditure and equilibrium output; government, fiscal policy and monetary policy; the demand for and supply of money and the equilibrium interest rate; the open economy; and the budget, the budget deficit and stabilization policy.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 7

question: what is acc 110 principles of accounting i about
answer: ACC 110 Principles of Accounting I: This course familiarizes students with the basic principles of accounting. Topics include an introduction to accounting and book keeping, the role of accounting in business, recording business transactions, source documents (invoices, receipts, vouchers and notes), the books used in accounting, double entry principles, balancing accounts and the trial balance, classification of accounts, the balance sheet, final accounts, depreciation, bad debts and other provisions, bank reconciliation statements and cash book adjustment, correction of errors, and incomplete records. It is scheduled in semester 1 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 7

question: what is acc 120 principles of accounting ii about
answer: ACC 120 Principles of Accounting II: This course builds on the accounting fundamentals of Accounting I and stresses practical applications and exercises. It covers the vertical presentation of final accounts, assets and liabilities, manufacturing accounts, accounts of non-profit organizations, consignment accounts, joint ventures, goods on sale or return, partnership accounts and dissolution of partnership, accounting for bills of exchange, accounting conventions and the problems of valuation and income determination, the form, content and interpretation of published accounts, an introduction to cash and funds flow statements, and an introduction to the problems of price level changes. It is scheduled in semester 3 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 8

question: what is eco 211/mgt 211 statistical methods for economics business statistics about
answer: ECO 211/MGT 211 Introduction to Statistical Methods for Economics 1/Business 1: This course introduces the definition and scope of statistics, descriptive statistics, probability theory, discrete and continuous probability distributions, sampling methods, sampling distributions, estimation and hypothesis testing, inference about a single population, and the comparison of two populations. It is scheduled in semester 1 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 8

question: what is eco 210/mgt 210 applied mathematics for economics business about
answer: ECO 210/MGT 210 Applied Mathematics for Economics/Business: This course covers the mathematical techniques used in business and finance: linear relationships (graphing, linear functions, break-even analysis, systems of linear equations and matrices, Gauss-Jordan elimination); matrices (multiplication and inverses); mathematics of finance (simple and compound interest, annuities, instalment loans, sinking funds and amortization); functions (polynomial, rational, exponential and logarithmic); the derivative and techniques of differentiation; applications of the derivative (graphing, curve sketching and optimization); integration (substitution, the definite integral and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus); and multivariable calculus (partial derivatives, local extrema, Lagrange multipliers and constrained optimization).
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 8

question: what is mkt 210 principles of marketing about
answer: MKT 210 Principles of Marketing: A beginning course in marketing. It covers the meaning of marketing and the marketing concept, the role and importance of marketing, market segmentation, and business environmental analysis (political, economic, socio-cultural, technological, legal, ecological and regulatory forces, plus SWOT analysis and analysis of customers, buyer behaviour and competitors). It also covers marketing decision-making and the marketing plan and strategies, the marketing mix (the 4Ps or 7Ps: product, price, promotion, physical distribution, people, processes and physical evidence), marketing research (including measures such as cost, sales volume, market share, ROI, customer satisfaction and retention, market surveys and forecasting), and current trends in marketing. It is scheduled in semester 3 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 8

question: what is psm 200 introduction to procurement and supply chain management about
answer: PSM 200 Introduction to Procurement and Supply Chain Management: This course explores common terms in procurement and supply, the context and evolution of purchasing and supply chain, the value for money concept, the five rights of procurement, the role of the procurement and supply function in organizations, the components of a supply chain, procurement policy and procedures, the relationship of procurement and supply chain to other functions in organizations, and organizing the procurement and supply chain function. It is scheduled in semester 3 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 14

question: what is psm 201 government procurement in the gambia about
answer: PSM 201 Theory of Government Procurement in The Gambia: The course provides a brief history of procurement in The Gambia, the legal framework and the institutional framework of the procurement system, the objectives of the procurement system, the procurement cycle of The Gambia, and corruption and strategies for combatting corruption in government procurement in The Gambia. Prerequisite: Introduction to Procurement and Supply Chain Management (PSM 200). It is scheduled in semester 4 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management. The semester table lists it as Government Procurement in The Gambia.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 14

question: what is psm 202 understanding the procurement environment about
answer: PSM 202 Understanding the Procurement Environment: On completion, students can identify the range of environments in which procurement and supply operates and the external factors that affect its success. The course covers the types of private sector organization (sole traders, partnerships, registered companies, incorporated and unincorporated companies, SMEs, multinational corporations), environmental scanning, PEST (political, economic, social and technological) and STEEPLED (social, technological, economic, environmental, political, legislation, ethical and demographic) criteria, competitive forces, the five forces model, and the product life cycle. It is scheduled in semester 4 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 14

question: what is psm 210 human resource issues in procurement about
answer: PSM 210 Human Resource Issues in Procurement: This course introduces human resource management, the role of the HR practitioner, human resource policies (meaning, policy areas, formulating and implementing HR policies), HRM procedures (grievance, disciplinary and redundancy procedures), the concept of employee voice (involvement and participation, purposes, forms, joint consultation and suggestion schemes), and the role of the procurement manager as a front-line manager. It is scheduled in semester 4 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 14

question: what is fin 220 financial management about
answer: FIN 220 Financial Management: This course exposes students to the nature and significance of finance and economic activity, the theory of financial management, the role of the accountant and the finance manager, sources and uses of funds (including by banks and the corporate sector), cash flow and funds flow, the investment cycle, capitalization (over- and under-capitalization), guidelines for good business, capital formation and the role of money and near money (liquidity), preparing a model balance sheet with stock and flow concepts, deriving financial ratios, short-, medium- and long-term financing and external sources, financing asset requirements, and managing capital and the debt trap. Prerequisite: ACC 110 and ACC 120. It is scheduled in semester 3 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 14

question: what is psm 300 practice of public procurement in the gambia gppa documents about
answer: PSM 300 The Practice of Public Procurement in The Gambia (Practice Based Skills: Preparation of GPPA Documents): The course translates theory into practice by developing students' skills in preparing the Annual Procurement Plan, the Annual Assets Disposal Plan, the Standard Bidding Document, the Evaluation Report, the Notification of Award, the Debriefing Report, the Contract Document, the Monthly Procurement Report, the Annual Procurement Report, and the other forms developed by the Gambia Public Procurement Authority (GPPA). It also introduces corruption and the strategies for combatting corruption in government procurement in The Gambia. Prerequisite: Theory of Government Procurement in The Gambia (PSM 201). It is scheduled in semester 5 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management. The semester table lists it as Practice Based Skills: Preparation of GPPA Documents.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 15

question: what is psm 304 sustainable procurement about
answer: PSM 304 Sustainable Procurement: The module introduces sustainability and corporate social responsibility (CSR), the impact of procurement and supply on the environment, the implications of CSR for the procurement and supply function, and the strategies for monitoring CSR in procurement and supply. Prerequisite: Procurement Ethics and Good Governance (PSM 311). It is scheduled in semester 5 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 15

question: what is psm 305 logistics and distribution management about
answer: PSM 305 Logistics and Distribution Management: Key elements: the meaning and role of logistics in the economy, the role of supply in logistics, supply's involvement in transportation, transportation modes and carriers, types of carriers, providers and service options, best value delivery decisions and key selection criteria, FOB terms and Incoterms, rates and pricing, documentation in freight shipments, expediting and tracing shipments, freight audits, delivery options for services (buyer versus supplier location, on-premise versus off-premise/web-based IT delivery), transportation and logistics strategy, and organization for logistics. It is scheduled in semester 6 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 15

question: what is psm 306 managerial decision making in procurement about
answer: PSM 306 Managerial Decision Making in Procurement: This course explains the theory of decision making for procurement and supply chain managers: the meaning and types of managerial decisions, decision-making under certainty, risk and uncertainty, and tools for effective decision-making. It also covers the rational decision-making model, the bounded rationality model, intuitive decision-making, Pareto analysis, decision trees, stakeholder mapping, SWOT analysis, and groups and group decision making. It is scheduled in semester 5 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 16

question: what is psm 307 inventory management about
answer: PSM 307 Inventory Management: This course covers inventory forecasting techniques, fixed-quantity models, fixed-period models, probabilistic models, the functions and forms of inventory, the costs of inventories, ABC classification, vendor- or supplier-managed inventory, lean supply, just-in-time (JIT) and Kanban systems, and managing supply chain inventories. It is scheduled in semester 8 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 16

question: what is psm 308 communication in procurement about
answer: PSM 308 Communication in Procurement: This course explains managerial communication and its scope for management, media and modes of communication, types of communication, barriers to communication, principles of effective communication, verbal and non-verbal communication, conversation, conducting meetings, seminars and conferences, and oral presentation. It also covers how conflict arises in procurement and supply (defining workplace conflict and its sources within and between organizations) and approaches to conflict resolution with stakeholders (clarifying roles and responsibilities, group cohesion and achieving stakeholder buy-in). It is scheduled in semester 5 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 16

question: what is psm 309 global purchasing and supply chain management about
answer: PSM 309 Global Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Students learn the meaning and importance of global supply, reasons for global purchasing, potential problem areas in global procurement and supply, selecting and managing offshore suppliers, global sourcing organizations, intermediaries in global sources, information sources for locating and evaluating offshore suppliers, the use of Incoterms (Groups E, F, C and D), tools for global supply (countertrade, foreign trade zones, bonded warehouses, Temporary Importation Bond and duty drawbacks), theories in international trade, and regional trading agreements. Prerequisite: The Practice of Public Procurement in The Gambia (PSM 300). It is scheduled in semester 7 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 16

question: what is psm 310 legal aspects in purchasing and supply chain management about
answer: PSM 310 Legal Aspects in Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: The course examines the legal authority of buyer and seller, personal liability, the authority of suppliers' representatives, warranties, title to purchased goods, cancellation of orders and breach of contract, common law and the purchase of services, the law of software contracts, e-commerce and the law, intellectual property laws, product liability, and alternative dispute resolution. It also gives overviews of the UNCITRAL Model Law on Procurement, the EU law on procurement, the Agreement on Government Procurement, and the procurement guidelines of the World Bank, the African Development Bank and the Millennium Challenge Corporation. It is scheduled in semester 6 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 16

question: what is psm 311 procurement ethics and good governance about
answer: PSM 311 Procurement Ethics and Good Governance: The course enables students to develop and apply ethical codes of conduct, consider the ethical dimensions of the procurement function, address potential conflicts of interest in procurement and supply operations, and understand key issues in corporate governance. It covers principles of ethics, principles of corporate governance, the general principles of procurement, developing a code of conduct in procurement, potential conflicts of interest, ethical considerations when sourcing from another country, organizational considerations leading to effective ethical procurement, and ethical considerations in the procurement cycle. Prerequisite: Introduction to Procurement (PSM 200). It is scheduled in semester 6 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 17

question: what is psm 312 e-procurement about
answer: PSM 312 E-Procurement (procurement software applications): The focus areas are the concept of e-procurement, barriers to implementing e-procurement in organizations, the various application software, the use of systems technology and databases and how they contribute to procurement and supply, the different types of systems for supplier selection, ordering and payment, and the essence of quality management in procurement and supply. It is scheduled in semester 8 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 17

question: what is psm 313 entrepreneurship development small business management about
answer: PSM 313 Entrepreneurship Development/Small Business Management: The curriculum's description of this course is incomplete. It also highlights the public procurement policy areas used to promote the development of small businesses, local industries and other disadvantaged groups in an economy: margin of preference schemes, set asides, lotting of bids, and bid securing declarations.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 17

question: what is psm 314 negotiation in purchasing and supply about
answer: PSM 314 Negotiation in Purchasing and Supply: This course equips students with negotiation skills in both domestic and international contexts. It looks at the meaning of negotiation, types of negotiation, negotiation styles and stages, power in negotiation, negotiation tactics, negotiation outcomes (win-win and win-lose), and cultural understanding in international negotiation (the Hofstede cross-cultural model). It is scheduled in semester 7 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 17

question: what is psm 315 quality and systems management in procurement and supply about
answer: PSM 315 Quality and Systems Management in Procurement and Supply: Students learn the concepts of quality and total quality management and identify the components of quality management in procurement and supply. Topics include the contributors to total quality management, the quality management cycle, quality control, costs of quality, quality measures, quality management approaches, and quality standards and awards programmes. It is scheduled in semester 8 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 18

question: what is acc 312 costing in procurement cost accounting about
answer: ACC 312 Costing in Procurement (Cost Accounting): This course looks at the concept of cost, types of cost, how suppliers establish price (the cost approach and the market approach), and cost management tools and techniques: Total Cost of Ownership, target pricing, the learning curve (manufacturing progress function), value engineering and value analysis, and activity-based costing. It is scheduled in semester 6 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management. The semester table lists it as Cost Accounting.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 18

question: what is mgt 311 project management about
answer: MGT 311 Project Management: The course covers the nature and characteristics of a project and the project life cycle; classification and types of projects; the project cycle and associated theories (Keeling's four phases, the World Bank project cycle and Rondinelli's twelve phases); project conceptualization and appraisal; feasibility studies and risk management; avoiding management pitfalls and project success factors; project resources (estimating needs, financing, scheduling, lead times, contracts for supply, lease or buy decisions and manpower planning); project management structures and the project matrix; the project team and team leadership; project planning and design (the logical framework, objectives and master plans); planning and control tools (the critical path/PERT chart, precedence diagrams, Gantt charts, decision trees, float and crashing); implementation and financing; communication, conflict and control with stakeholders; supervision, monitoring, evaluation and review; project completion or termination and completion reports (IFAD and ADB formats); diffusion of project outputs; post-project follow-up; and writing project proposals. It is scheduled in semester 5 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 18

question: what is psm 316 contract management in procurement about
answer: PSM 316 Contract Management in Procurement: The module covers the nature and elements of a contract, the objectives of contract management, the contract management cycle and instruments, and possible supplier strategies. It also covers the procurement life cycle (plan, conduct and control procurements) from the perspective of both buyers and sellers, preparing and responding to RFPs, contract types, pricing mechanisms (such as firm fixed fees, penalty clauses and time and materials) and their implementation, outsourcing methodologies, global contracting, and the ethical challenges that arise in contract management. It is scheduled in semester 8 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 19

question: what is psm 317 introduction to procurement of services about
answer: PSM 317 Introduction to Procurement of Services: The module introduces the procurement of services: the importance and process of purchasing services, the make or buy decision in services procurement, the value of service purchasing (the Ellram and Tate model), challenges in purchasing services, sourcing strategies, contract management in purchasing services, and the skills required in purchasing services. It is scheduled in semester 7 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 19

question: what is psm 318 operations management about
answer: PSM 318 Operations Management: The course covers the fundamentals of performance analysis for operational issues in real supply chain processes: demand forecasting techniques, sales and operations planning, mathematical programming applications and spreadsheet solutions, supply chain inventory planning, uncertainty and safety stock management, project resource allocation and risk analysis, network design and facility location selection, and computer simulation and quality management. Business cases on cost-effective solutions are used to build analytical thinking and knowledge of performance optimization toward operational excellence of supply chains. It is scheduled in semester 7 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 20

question: what is psm 319 stakeholder relationships management in procurement and supply about
answer: PSM 319 Stakeholder Relationships Management in Procurement and Supply: Procurement and supply is built on relationships with internal and external stakeholders. The module defines and profiles external stakeholders (suppliers, customers, consumers, communities, government and other groups, and the distinction between customers and consumers) and identifies internal stakeholders involved in purchases and deliveries, including the role of procurement and supply in dealing with marketing, sales, production, operations, human resources, finance, design and development, distribution, facilities, senior management and the board. It is scheduled in semester 7 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 20

question: what is psm 410 strategic procurement management about
answer: PSM 410 Strategic Procurement Management: The course examines how organizations establish long-term direction, set performance objectives, develop strategies to achieve them in light of internal and external circumstances, and execute the chosen action plans. It covers defining the organization's business and developing a strategic mission, establishing strategic objectives and targeted results, implementing and executing the plan, and evaluating strategic performance and making corrective adjustments. It is scheduled in semester 7 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 20

question: what is eco 224 quantitative methods about
answer: ECO 224 Quantitative Methods: Introduction to and the nature of quantitative analysis; probability concepts and game theory; decision theory models, decision trees, utility theory and prospect theory; linear and non-linear programming; inventory control models; transportation and assignment models; network models including PERT and the Critical Path Method; an introduction to project management; and waiting lines and queuing theory. Prerequisite: ECO 210 and ECO 211. It is described in the curriculum but does not appear in the semester tables.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 21

question: what is mgt 320 research methodology about
answer: MGT 320 Research Methodology: This course examines the principles and techniques used in designing and conducting academic research in the management sciences: the need for and uses of management research, the philosophical and conceptual bases of scientific research, criteria for researchable topics, defining the research problem, research alternatives, design of the research instrument, collection, coding, analysis and interpretation of data, report writing and referencing methods. It is scheduled in semester 5 and semester 6 of the BSc in Procurement and Supply Chain Management.
source: UTG School of Business and Public Administration - BSc Procurement and Supply Chain Management Curriculum (Department of Management Sciences, January 2021), p. 21

question: what is psm 491 final year project paper dissertation about
answer: PSM 491 Final Year Project Paper / Dissertation (ACC 491 in the semester table): This course carries out the research plans, including collecting and analyzing data, and the student prepares a research report to submit at the end of the semester. question: is there a bsc economics degree programme at utg and what is its framework
answer: The BSc Economics programme framework (DEMS) runs over 8 semesters. Semesters 1 to 6 and 8 are 18 credit hours each and semester 7 is 21 credit hours.
